intro.hive: from building the network to paying the seller
intro.aladdin: from a seller signing up to getting paid
intro.accounts: from signing in to exporting invoices and reports

steps.title: Draw the map of the organisation
steps.text: Create regions, then clusters inside them, then hubs inside clusters. Each hub gets a type (ISD / OSD / sub area), a tier and whether it is a sorting hub.

steps.title: Define the delivery area
steps.text: Under each hub: cities, zones, areas and sectors. Zone boundaries are drawn on a map. Routes group a hub's zones and get a default agent.

steps.title: Connect hubs with linehauls
steps.text: Linehauls are the trunk lines between hubs and sorting centres. Sub-sort centres get PTN racks whose pigeon holes map to hubs or linehauls.

steps.title: Hire staff and give access
steps.text: Staff accounts, teams, departments, roles and permission scopes decide who sees which page. Staff log in by SSO and pick their hub, and check in daily.

steps.title: Onboard riders
steps.text: Riders (called agents in code) apply, are approved, get salary or commission types, holidays and attendance.

steps.title: Set up money rails and premises
steps.text: Register the banks (with branches) and mobile wallets sellers can be paid into, and the landlords of rented hubs.

steps.title: Acquire the seller
steps.text: Referral QR codes and short links bring new sellers in. Large accounts are created directly as corporate merchants.

steps.title: Verify who they are
steps.text: Check the seller's identity documents (KYC) and profile.

steps.title: Configure the business
steps.text: Set the business type (prepaid, postpaid, corporate), service options and a key account manager. Price plans set delivery fees, extra charges and slabs; discounts need approval.

steps.title: Approve pickup stores
steps.text: The seller's stores (pickup and return addresses) are reviewed, assigned to the right hub, and their map location is verified.

steps.title: Approve the payout account
steps.text: When a seller adds or changes the bank or wallet they are paid into, finance approves it.

steps.title: Order arrives
steps.text: The seller books the order in aladdin or via API. In hive it shows up in the order search. Orders missing data land in the incomplete list to be fixed.

steps.title: Pickup is requested
steps.text: "Collect N parcels from store X." KAMs can create the request on the seller's behalf.

steps.title: Pickup is planned
steps.text: Waiting pickups are grouped by store and route, and an agent is assigned.

steps.title: Parcels are collected
steps.text: The agent visits the stores and brings parcels to the first-mile hub, then the pickup run is closed. Or the seller drops parcels at the hub, verified by OTP.

hive.title: First-mile hub
hive.when: The hub where the parcel enters

steps.title: Check in and sort
steps.text: Parcels are weighed, matched to their order and sorted per destination. The consignment log shows every scan.

steps.title: Handle surprises
steps.text: A parcel with no order in the system is a no-entry: create the order, process it or return it. Missing labels are printed centrally.

steps.title: Pack baskets
steps.text: Sorted parcels go into sealed baskets with a printed label. A basket moves as one unit from here on.

steps.title: Dispatch a transfer run
steps.text: Baskets are attached to a transfer run along a linehaul, with a printed gate pass.

steps.title: Receive and reconcile
steps.text: Baskets are received by scan. Anything that should be there but isn't, or arrived unexpectedly, goes to missing/extra.

steps.title: Central and sub-sort
steps.text: The central warehouse and sub-sort centres route each parcel to its last-mile hub, correcting the hub if needed, using PTN racks.

steps.title: Arrive at last-mile hub
steps.text: The parcel reaches the hub that will deliver it.

hive.title: Last mile delivery
hive.when: To the buyer's door · status 14 → final

steps.title: Build the delivery run
steps.text: Parcels are scanned into an agent's delivery run. They can be moved to another zone or hub, reassigned, or marked lost or damaged.

steps.title: Rider delivers and collects cash
steps.text: Outcome is delivered, partial delivery, exchange, hold, paid return or return. The buyer pays the COD amount in cash.

steps.title: Approve exceptions
steps.text: When an agent asks to change an outcome (return, price change, exchange, partial), QC or the seller approves it. QC also flags fake requests per hub and agent.

steps.title: Fix a status by hand
steps.text: When the normal flow can't, statuses are changed in bulk.

steps.title: Rate the riders
steps.text: Customers and sellers rate agents. Hub summaries and weekly trends show who is doing well.

steps.title: Report fraud
steps.text: Sellers report buyers who refuse or cheat. Ops approve or reject the report.

steps.title: Return to the seller
steps.text: Returned parcels travel back through baskets and transfers to the first-mile hub, then a return run hands them to the seller.

steps.title: Reverse pickup from the buyer
steps.text: For exchanges and customer returns, an agent collects the item from the buyer.

steps.title: Parcel is lost
steps.text: Mark it lost and decide who pays the compensation: the agent, the hub or Carrybee.

steps.title: Close the run and count cash
steps.text: The agent hands over the cash; it's counted note by note (1000, 500, 200…). If the agent app never ended the run, a manager force-closes it.

steps.title: Chase unclosed runs
steps.text: Runs never closed mean cash not accounted for. They are listed here.

steps.title: Hub cash book
steps.text: The ledger tracks cash in hand vs carried forward per hub.

steps.title: Hub deposits COD
steps.text: The hub deposits the collected cash, minus expenses and money lost, with proof. Payable consignments show which delivered orders the money belongs to.

steps.title: Chase missing deposits
steps.text: Hubs that collected but haven't deposited are flagged.

steps.title: Finance approves deposits
steps.text: Each deposit is approved or rejected, one by one or in bulk. The hub dashboard shows the per-hub money picture.

steps.title: Generate the invoice
steps.text: From delivered orders: COD collected minus delivery fee and COD fee = what the seller gets. Regular or positive-balance invoices, or one-off custom invoices.

steps.title: Pay it
steps.text: Unpaid invoices are exported as a bank Excel file, moved into processing (RTGS tagged), and marked paid.

steps.title: Pay early on request
steps.text: Sellers can ask to be paid now instead of waiting for the cycle.

steps.title: Receivable invoices
steps.text: When fees exceed the COD collected (for example a postpaid account), the seller owes Carrybee. Monthly invoices are generated and payments recorded.

steps.title: Pay riders' allowance
steps.text: Distance-based delivery allowance for agents, paid with an OTP step.

steps.title: Hub expenses and rent
steps.text: Petty cash and rent claims go through ops head → HR → audit → accounts, then are withdrawn by OTP.

steps.title: Approve claims
steps.text: Allowance and expense claims are reconciled through cluster lead → region lead → HR → audit → accounts.

steps.title: Measure the business
steps.text: Dashboards for agent productivity, delivery outcomes, merchant churn, hub backlog and open runs. CSV reports for deeper analysis.

steps.title: Audit and repair
steps.text: The activity log shows who changed what. G-Mode reopens runs, resets OTPs, regenerates invoices and impersonates users to fix problems.

steps.title: Keep people informed
steps.text: In-app notifications for staff and push notifications sent from the panel.

steps.title: Sign up with a phone number
steps.text: Register with name and phone, confirm the OTP sent by SMS, then log in with phone and password. Forgot password also uses OTP. Support staff can impersonate a seller to help them.

steps.title: Complete the personal profile
steps.text: Add personal details and identity documents (NID or birth certificate) so Carrybee can verify who the seller is. Change the password here too.

steps.title: Create a business
steps.text: Create a business with a category and sub-category. One login can own several businesses and switch between them; every other page is scoped to the chosen business.

steps.title: Learn the basics
steps.text: Common questions about pricing, pickups, payments and returns.

steps.title: Add pickup stores
steps.text: Add the addresses where Carrybee collects parcels and returns failed ones, on a map. Each store is linked to a hub and route. Pick a default pickup and return store. Carrybee ops approve new stores.

steps.title: Choose how to get paid
steps.text: Add a bank account or mobile wallet (MFS such as bKash or Nagad) and the payout schedule: regular, custom, or on demand. Changes are approved by Carrybee finance.

steps.title: Invite the team
steps.text: Add staff to the business as operator or accountant, each with their own permissions.

steps.title: Connect a website (optional)
steps.text: Get API credentials, set webhooks for order events, and read the API docs to create orders straight from the seller's own shop.

steps.title: Check the buyer first
steps.text: Look up the buyer's phone number in the fraud checker to see if others have reported them for refusing parcels.

steps.title: Create orders
steps.text: One at a time, in bulk from a spreadsheet, from a photo using AI/OCR, or through the API. Each order gets a consignment ID, a COD amount to collect, and a delivery price calculated from weight and area.

steps.title: Print labels
steps.text: Print the POD label (barcode + QR code) and stick it on each parcel.

steps.title: Request a pickup
steps.text: Choose the store and how many parcels are ready. A Carrybee rider is assigned to collect them.

steps.title: See pickup history
steps.text: Each request shows how many parcels were ordered, actually picked and sorted at the hub, and its status.

aladdin.title: Track the parcel
aladdin.when: While it moves · sorted → in_transit → received_at_lmh → assigned_for_delivery

steps.title: Follow every order
steps.text: Order list grouped as active, delivered, returning and returned, with full history per order. Buyers can track publicly with the consignment ID. While moving, the seller can edit, cancel, ask to hold, or ask for urgent delivery.

steps.title: Get notified
steps.text: In-app and push notifications for returns, urgent approvals, invoices and no-entry parcels, with do-not-disturb settings.

steps.title: Talk to the rider
steps.text: Live chat with the delivery agent about one parcel, for example to share directions.

steps.title: See today at a glance
steps.text: The dashboard shows order progress, delivery split, payments due and recent orders.

aladdin.title: Handle problems
aladdin.when: When delivery doesn't go to plan

steps.title: Answer the high alert queue
steps.text: Riders ask the seller to approve a change: return, price change, exchange, partial delivery or paid return. Also listed: partial deliveries, returns on the way, parcels with no order (no-entry) and last-mile delivery issues.

steps.title: Fix the order
steps.text: Send a returned parcel to another customer, reopen a cancelled pickup, or create an exchange or reverse pickup to get an item back from the buyer.

steps.title: Report a bad buyer
steps.text: File a fraud report against a buyer. Carrybee ops approve or reject it.

steps.title: Rate the rider
steps.text: Rate the pickup or delivery agent. Ratings feed hive's rating management.

steps.title: Read the numbers
steps.text: Order trends over time, overall statistics and the best-performing stores.

steps.title: Read the invoice
steps.text: Each invoice shows COD collected, minus delivery fee and COD fee, plus any compensation, giving the amount Carrybee pays. Download as PDF or CSV.

steps.title: Withdraw early
steps.text: On-demand payout: ask to be paid now instead of waiting for the cycle.

steps.title: Pay what you owe
steps.text: If fees are more than the cash collected, the seller owes Carrybee and pays through bKash, Nagad, SSLCommerz or bank transfer.

steps.title: Log in with OTP
steps.text: Staff log in with phone and a one-time code. What they see depends on two permissions: revenue recognition (invoices) and legal panel (orders). Without either they land on a no-access page.

steps.title: Lookup data for filters
steps.text: Lists of users, hubs, departments and teams are loaded to fill dropdowns. These modules have no pages of their own; the users page is planned but not built yet.

steps.title: Look up a business
steps.text: Read-only list of seller businesses with their COD and return fees, payout frequency, KAM and wallet.

steps.title: Check identity status
steps.text: Sellers and their eKYC verification status.

steps.title: Export merchant invoices
steps.text: The invoices hive generated for each seller: what was collected, Carrybee's fees, and what was paid out. Export a summary, per-merchant or per-order CSV, or a single invoice as PDF for the books.

steps.title: Review orders by parcel type
steps.text: Delivered consignments with amounts collected, fees, hubs, recipient and transfer status, filterable by parcel type and exportable as CSV. A CSV upload to set parcel types exists but is switched off.

steps.title: Download reports
steps.text: Consignment-wise CSV report. Custom and merchant reports exist in code but are hidden from the menu.
